editorial:
Imagine taking a long walk in the woods with your family, but instead of just hiking, you start asking the big questions about where we go when we die. That is exactly what happens to six-year-old Sam in this story. You get to see the world through his eyes, which makes everything feel fresh and a bit magical. The vibe is very calm and peaceful, focusing on the small things in nature and the bond between a father and son. It feels like a warm hug, but it also makes you think about the sad parts of life in a way that is easy to handle.

The kid acting here is the real star because he feels like a real child, not a scripted actor. While the story moves slowly, the beautiful scenery makes it worth your time. If you are in the mood for something loud and fast, this is not for you, but it is perfect for a quiet night in.
endingExplained: At the very end, Sam finds a dead bird and helps his dad bury it. This simple act helps him realize that death is just a natural part of life, like leaves falling in autumn. He stops being afraid and accepts that everything has a cycle. The movie wraps up with the family finishing their trip, showing that while loss is hard, the love they share keeps them moving forward together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about family and nature.
